synthesis: The simple-zero argument adds a certification constraint to the total critical-line zero framework: after the general reduction counts zeros of Re eta, simple zeros are obtained only by subtracting zeros of eta and imposing a degree-one choice of Q so that surviving Re eta zeros imply xi=0 but xi' is nonzero. That restriction narrows the differential family used in the mean-value functional, forcing the simple-zero numerical optimization to be performed separately from the less constrained total-zero choice.
